description.value: A randomized crossover fMRI study examined how an acute bout of moderate-intensity exercise versus sedentary activity altered children's neural responses to high- and low-calorie food pictures.

spans.text: Using a randomized cross-over design, 26 healthy weight children completed two separate laboratory conditions (exercise; sedentary).

value: The whole-brain ANOVA revealed significant clusters of activation indicating a main effect of exercise condition in the left postcentral gyrus and the right insula. There was less activity in the left postcentral gyrus following the exercise condition than following the sedentary condition, while there was greater activity in the right anterior insula following the exercise condition than following the sedentary condition.
Relative to the sedentary condition, our results showed decreased activation of the post-central gyrus following exercise and increased activation of the right anterior insula following exercise.

value: We observed two regions where there was an interaction between activity level and stimulus type in fMRI activation; one in the right medial temporal lobe (including right hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus) and one in the left hippocampus. In both regions, there was greater activation in response to high- compared to low-calorie food stimuli following exercise.
An acute bout of exercise results in greater activation to high-calorie and reduced activation to low-calorie pictures of food in both the left hippocampus and right medial temporal lobe.

spans.text: We observed two regions where there was an interaction between activity level and stimulus type in fMRI activation; one in the right medial temporal lobe (including right hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus; F (1,25) = 23.52; p < 0.001) and one in the left hippocampus (F (1,25) = 14.06; p < 0.001).

The protocol included: a 3-min warm-up, 3 min of walking at 3.0 mph, and 0.5% increase in grade every minute until each participant reached a steady state HR of ~ 135 bpm; thereafter, speed and grade were maintained.
